# Exact slab first variation and a genuine-contact failure of credit monotonicity
by root and independently verifies it from vertical sections. The source
geometry is `candidate 2bf98ea275da010b`.

All the examples below are actual convex-body mixed-integer intersections
with two globally deepest contacts, a critical three-cap circuit at one
contact and a critical two-cap circuit at the other, and no fiber of half
the total mass. They show that transverse erosion alone does not force
monotonicity of either the three-cap surplus or, with a steeper original
critical cap, the three-cap credit itself. They do not contradict OC.

## 1. The actual body and its global halfspace depth

Use coordinates `(z,x,y)` in `R x R^2` and put

    K = {(x,y): |x|+|y| <= 1},
    C = [-1,2] x K,
    S = {-1,0,1,2} x K.

The continuous fibers have area `|K|=2`, so `H_2(S)=8`. The body is
full-dimensional and the displayed four fibers are all its integer
fibers. In particular each fiber has area `2 < H_2(S)/2`.

Both `(0,0,0)` and `(1,0,0)` have raw halfspace depth at least 3. To see
this at the first point, translate any containing halfspace parallel to
itself until its boundary passes through the point. If its continuous
normal `v` is nonzero, its traces on the fibers at -1 and 1 have total
area 2: their thresholds are opposite, and K is centrally symmetric.
Its trace on the fiber at 0 has area 1. The remaining fiber contributes
nonnegatively. All these continuous hyperplane boundaries have area
zero. The same argument at the point over 1 uses the fibers at 0 and 2.
A pure-integer closed halfspace through either point has mass at least
4, including its complete boundary fiber. Thus the argument covers all
closed ambient containing halfspaces, including boundary mass.

At the contact over 1 consider

    P_+ = { x + (z-1)/2 >= 0 },
    P_- = {-x + (z-1)/2 >= 0 }.

Each has total mass 3. Indeed the fiber at -1 contributes zero area,
the fiber at 1 contributes 1, and the fibers at 0 and 2 together
contribute 2. These are opposite-normal critical caps.

For any real `L >= 1/2`, at the contact over 0 consider

    G_1 = { x - L z >= 0 },
    G_2 = { y - z/2 >= 0 },
    G_3 = {-x-y - z/2 >= 0 }.                       (1)

Each has total mass 3. Its own fiber contributes 1. Its two traces over
-1 and 1 have total area 2 by central symmetry, even when L is larger
than the support value of K. The trace over 2 is empty or supporting
and hence has area zero, since `h_K(1,0)=h_K(0,1)=h_K(-1,-1)=1`
and each corresponding slope is at least 1/2.

The three continuous normals in (1) positively sum to zero, and the
sum of their affine margins is `-(L+1)z`. Thus their union covers the
entire plane at every `z <= 0`. The pair `P_+,P_-` covers the entire
plane at every `z >= 1`. These five caps cover S. Consequently every
point of S belongs to a cap of total mass 3, and its depth is at most
3. The maximum raw depth is therefore exactly

    Q = 3,       Q/H_2(S) = 3/8.

In particular all five displayed caps are genuinely critical at the
stated deepest contacts. This is an example above the OC target
`(1/2)(2/3)^2=2/9`, not a counterexample to that target.

## 2. The normalized pair residual, with equality in transverse erosion

Write

    z(t) = -t/(1-t),      0 <= t < 1/2.

The closed complement of the pair on a fiber with `z<1` is the slab
`|x| <= (1-z)/2`, up to its two null boundaries. Its projectively
normalized residual is

    D_t = (1-t)K intersect {|x| <= 1/2}.

This parameterization describes actual real sections of C and does not
replace the mixed-integer sum by an integral. In particular, the
computations below are local geometric identities for the normalized
residual; no unproved discrete-to-continuous summation is made.

The transverse body provided by the other contact is

    E = K intersect {x=0} = {0} x [-1,1].

For `0 < t < 1/2`, the vertical sections of D_t on `I=[-1/2,1/2]` are

    [-(1-t)+|x|, (1-t)-|x|].                         (2)

Therefore, whenever `0 <= epsilon <= t`,

    D_t + epsilon E = D_(t-epsilon).                (3)

Thus the inclusion from the slab erosion theorem is an equality in
this example. Its area is

    V(t) = |D_t| = 3/2 - 2t.                        (4)

Under the normalization, the original caps (1) have traces

    x >= -Lt,       y >= -t/2,       x+y <= t/2.     (5)

Moving toward the contact, from t to `t-epsilon`, therefore expands
D_t by the minimal transverse extrusion (3) while moving these three
original cap thresholds. Keeping the thresholds artificially fixed
would be a different deformation.

## 3. Exact captured areas

Let A_i(t) be the area captured by the ith cap in (5) inside D_t.
For `0<t<min(1/3,1/(2L))`, direct vertical integration gives

    A_1(t) = 3/4 + (2L-1)t - (L^2+2L)t^2,
    A_2(t) = 3/4 - t/2,
    A_3(t) = 3/4 - t/2 - t^2/2.                    (6)

Here are the integration ranges, so the formulas do not depend on
numerical clipping. Put `r=1-t`. For the first cap, integrate
`2(r-|x|)` from `-Lt` to `1/2`. For the second, the threshold `-t/2`
lies strictly between the two endpoints in (2) for every x in I;
integrate `r-|x|+t/2` over I. For the third, put

    a = -1/2 + 3t/4,        b = 1/2 - t/4.

The entire section is captured on `[-1/2,a]`. On the two subsequent
intervals the captured lengths are

    x in [a,0]:  captured length = r+t/2,
    x in [0,b]:  captured length = r+t/2-2x.

Thus a fully explicit formula for the third area is

    integral_(-1/2)^a 2(r+x) dx
      + integral_a^0 (r+t/2) dx
      + integral_0^b (r+t/2-2x) dx.

It evaluates to A_3 in (6). No section is captured on `[b,1/2]`.

For the two parameter choices used below, A_3 is the unique minimum
when t>0 in the stated range. For `L=1/2`,

    A_1-A_3 = t/2 - 3t^2/4 > 0   for 0<t<1/3.

For `L=10`,

    A_1-A_3 = (39t-239t^2)/2 > 0 for 0<t<1/20.

In both cases `A_2-A_3=t^2/2>0`.

## 4. The surplus decreases even for the smallest critical slopes

The ordinary planar three-cap credit is

    F(t) = A_1(t)+A_2(t)+A_3(t) - (3/4) min_i A_i(t).

The coefficient is exact: `Gamma_2=4/9` and
`3-1/Gamma_2=3/4`. For `L=1/2` and `0<t<1/3`, formulas (4)--(6) give

    A_1 = 3/4 - 5t^2/4,
    A_2 = 3/4 - t/2,
    A_3 = 3/4 - t/2 - t^2/2,
    F   = 27/16 - 5t/8 - 11t^2/8,
    F-V = 3/16 + (11/8)t(1-t).                     (7)

Consequently the right derivative in the direction toward the anchor
is

    d/depsilon [F(t-epsilon)-V(t-epsilon)] at 0+
        = -(11/8)(1-2t).

At `t=1/4` this is `-11/16`. The surplus strictly decreases despite
equality in transverse erosion. The credit F itself has derivative
`21/16` at this point; the area V has derivative 2. These two distinct
quantities must not be conflated.

The part of D_t lying in all three original caps is the triangle

    x >= -t/2,  y >= -t/2,  x+y <= t/2.

Its vertices are `(-t/2,-t/2)`, `(t,-t/2)`, and `(-t/2,t)`. The
triangle lies inside D_t for `0<t<1/3`, and its area is `9t^2/8`.
It also strictly shrinks toward the anchor; at `t=1/4` its derivative
in epsilon is `-9/16`.

## 5. The credit itself can decrease for an original critical cap

Now choose `L=10`. All original criticality and contact facts in
Section 1 still hold. For `0<t<1/20`,

    A_1 = 3/4 + 19t - 120t^2,
    A_2 = 3/4 - t/2,
    A_3 = 3/4 - t/2 - t^2/2,
    F   = 27/16 + (147/8)t - (961/8)t^2,
    F-V = 3/16 + (163/8)t - (961/8)t^2.             (8)

At `t=1/40`, the derivatives toward the anchor are exactly

    d/depsilon F(t-epsilon) at 0+       = -1979/160,
    d/depsilon (F-V)(t-epsilon) at 0+   = -2299/160.

In particular both are strictly negative. The earlier unsaved number
`-1979/160` belongs to F, not to F-V.

For completeness, the intersection of the three caps is the triangle
with vertices `(-Lt,-t/2)`, `(t,-t/2)`, and `(-Lt,(L+1/2)t)` whenever
that triangle lies inside D_t. Its area is

    ((L+1)^2/2)t^2.

For `L=10`, containment holds for `0<t<2/43`, which includes a
neighborhood of `1/40`. Its derivative there is `-121/40`.

## 6. Exact first variation for a general planar transverse extrusion

The following elementary formula records all cut coincidences and
zero-area intermediate intersections. It is useful because a formula
which counts only cap-section motion and omits exposed boundary
motion, or which chooses one minimizer before differentiating, can
give the wrong sign.

**Theorem.** Let D be a nonempty compact convex subset of the plane
whose projection on the first coordinate is a nondegenerate interval
`I=[a,b]`. Write its sections as `[l(x),u(x)]`, allowing `l=u`, and
let `E={0} x [e_-,e_+]` with `e_-<=e_+`. For epsilon>=0 put

    D_epsilon = D + epsilon E.

Let a finite family of moving closed halfplanes be given by

    p_i x + q_i y >= h_i + k_i epsilon,
    (p_i,q_i) != (0,0).                            (9)

Let A(epsilon) be the area of their intersection with D_epsilon.
The following construction gives its right derivative at zero.

For `q_i>0`, put

    alpha_i(x)=(h_i-p_i x)/q_i,   v_i=k_i/q_i,

and include this as a lower section bound. For `q_i<0` use the same
formulas and include it as an upper section bound. Include l as a
lower bound with velocity e_-, and u as an upper bound with velocity
e_+. Thus

    L_0(x)=max(lower bounds at zero),
    U_0(x)=min(upper bounds at zero),
    L_dot(x)=max(velocities among active lower bounds),
    U_dot(x)=min(velocities among active upper bounds).

Set `g_0(x)=(U_0(x)-L_0(x))_+` and define

    g_dot(x) = U_dot(x)-L_dot(x)    if U_0(x)>L_0(x),
               0                  if U_0(x)<L_0(x),
               (U_dot(x)-L_dot(x))_+ if U_0(x)=L_0(x).     (10)

The active-bound prescriptions in this formula are essential even
when a cap boundary agrees with an edge of D along an interval, or
two moving cuts coincide at zero.

The vertical cuts `q_i=0` restrict the x coordinate. Include a as a
lower endpoint bound with velocity zero and b as an upper endpoint
bound with velocity zero. A cut with `p_i>0` gives a lower bound
`h_i/p_i` of velocity `k_i/p_i`; a cut with `p_i<0` gives an upper
bound with the same formulas. Define

    a_0=max(lower endpoint bounds),
    b_0=min(upper endpoint bounds),
    a_dot=max(velocities among active lower endpoint bounds),
    b_dot=min(velocities among active upper endpoint bounds).

Then the exact right derivative is

    A'(0+) = 0                                           if a_0>b_0,

    A'(0+) = (b_dot-a_dot)_+ g_0(a_0)                    if a_0=b_0,

    A'(0+) = integral_(a_0)^(b_0) g_dot(x) dx
             + b_dot g_0(b_0) - a_dot g_0(a_0)          if a_0<b_0. (11)

The endpoint evaluations in the last two cases are within I. The
theorem applies to one cap as well as to an arbitrary finite
intersection, including the three-cap core above. If the projection
of D is a singleton, D_epsilon also has zero area for every epsilon,
so the derivative is zero and no section formula is needed.

**Proof.** Compact convexity implies that l is a finite convex lower
semicontinuous function and u a finite concave upper semicontinuous
function on I. They are continuous up to the endpoints. For example,
convex interpolation between an endpoint and a fixed interior point
gives the appropriate upper bound on l near that endpoint, while
lower semicontinuity gives the reverse bound. The proof for u is the
same with signs reversed. Both functions have bounded variation on I.

The section of D_epsilon at x is exactly
`[l(x)+epsilon e_-,u(x)+epsilon e_+]`. Hence Fubini gives

    A(epsilon) = integral_(a(epsilon))^(b(epsilon))
                   (U_epsilon(x)-L_epsilon(x))_+ dx       (12)

when `a(epsilon)<=b(epsilon)`, and zero otherwise, where L_epsilon
is the maximum of the lower affine-in-epsilon bounds and U_epsilon
is the minimum of the upper bounds. Likewise a(epsilon) is the maximum
of the finitely many affine lower endpoint bounds and b(epsilon) is
the minimum of the upper ones.

For each fixed x, a maximum of finitely many affine functions has
right derivative equal to the maximum of their slopes among the
maximizers at zero. A minimum has the corresponding minimum slope.
The right derivative of the positive part at zero is the positive
part of the right derivative. This proves (10), including all ties.
All these functions are uniformly Lipschitz in epsilon, with a bound
depending only on the finitely many velocities, so bounded dominated
convergence justifies integration of (10) over any fixed subinterval.

Near epsilon=0+, finite maxima and minima of affine endpoint functions
are themselves affine, with respective slopes a_dot and b_dot. If
the initial endpoint gap is negative, it stays negative. If the
endpoints coincide, their interval has length
`epsilon (b_dot-a_dot)_+` for sufficiently small positive epsilon.
Continuity of g_0 and uniform `O(epsilon)` change of the integrand give
the middle formula in (11). In the positive-length case the two
endpoint strips give the boundary terms in (11), using the one-sided
traces of the continuous bounded-variation section function g_0.
Their integrand changes contribute only `O(epsilon^2)`. The fixed
interior contributes the integral of (10). This proves every case of
(11). No interchange with an unbounded derivative or omission of a
positive boundary length is involved. QED.

For a single nonvertical lower cut `y>=alpha(x)+v epsilon`, at a
positive-length section where `l<alpha<u` the integrand derivative is
`e_+-v`. Where the entire section is captured it is `e_+-e_-`. At a
positive-length section with the cut agreeing with the lower edge it
is `e_+-max(e_-,v)`, and with the cut agreeing with the upper edge it is
`(e_+-v)_+`. At a collapsed section with `l=u=alpha`, both bounds are
active and the derivative is `(e_+-max(e_-,v))_+`, as in (10). These
are useful special cases; simply assigning a generic crossing formula
to a coincident edge would fail.

For example, let D be the unit square and E the vertical interval
`[-1,1]`. The moving cut `y>=-2 epsilon` contains all the extruded
square, and its area derivative is 2. Its initial boundary agrees
with the lower edge of D. The generic interior-crossing expression
`e_+-(-2)=3` is wrong; the active-bound formula gives
`1-max(-1,-2)=2`. Similarly the cut `y>=1+2 epsilon`, coinciding
initially with the upper edge, gives derivative zero rather than -1.

## 7. Active minima of cap areas

If finitely many areas have expansions

    A_i(epsilon)=A_i(0)+epsilon a_i+o(epsilon),

write `I_min={i:A_i(0)=min_j A_j(0)}`. Then

    d/depsilon min_i A_i(epsilon) at 0+
         = min_(i in I_min) a_i.                       (13)

Indeed the positive gap to any inactive index excludes it for small
epsilon, and the finitely many remainder terms are uniformly
`o(epsilon)`. Therefore, for any fixed real r,

    d/depsilon [sum_i A_i(epsilon)-r min_i A_i(epsilon)] at 0+
         = sum_i a_i - r min_(i in I_min) a_i.           (14)

This conclusion requires neither a unique minimizing cap nor stable
labels through a tie. Subtracting the derivative of `|D_epsilon|`
gives the surplus derivative. In the transverse extrusion above,

    |D_epsilon|' at 0+ = (e_+-e_-)(b-a),

exactly, including an initially lower-dimensional D with nonzero
projection width. Applying (11) and (14) with `E=[-1,1]` and the
threshold velocities from (5) reproduces (7)--(8).

For instance, at `L=1/2,t=1/4`, the three captured-area derivatives
are `5/8,1/2,3/4`. The unique minimum is A_3, so the credit derivative
is `5/8+1/2+3/4-(3/4)(3/4)=21/16`. The area derivative is 2, giving
the stated surplus derivative `-11/16`. At `L=10,t=1/40`, the three
derivatives are `-13,1/2,21/40`; the same formula gives `-1979/160`.

## 8. Scope of the conclusion

The valid slab inclusion, its sharp volume gain, and the original-cap
missed-residual inclusions in the source all remain intact. In this
example the slab inclusion is an equality, so strengthening that
inclusion to an exact extrusion would not restore the proposed
monotonicities. Neither the full three-cap credit nor its surplus over
the residual area has a universal favorable directional sign under
this deformation. An argument seeking global 3+2 compensation must
retain further information or a different aggregate quantity.

The companion exact-arithmetic verifier is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_two_contact_slab_credit_first_variation.py`. Its finite checks
audit the displayed algebra and degeneracy cases; the proofs here do
not depend on those checks and assert no global OC conclusion.
